title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Registration Data
description: Parent user shares highly sensitive data (govt ID, password, six-digit code) without adequate controls, risking unauthorized disclosure to third parties during registration process.

title: Lack of Control Over Data Usage After Sharing
description: Parent user may not have control over how their shared registration data (email, name, govt ID) is used, stored, or shared further by the authentication service.

title: Data Deception via Metadata in Transit
description: Data in transit (DF1) may contain metadata about the parties (parent user, authentication service) that could be used to link or identify them, potentially enabling profiling or tracking.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure by Authentication Service
description: Authentication service may disclose the received registration data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) to unauthorized third parties or for purposes beyond registration.

title: Unintended Consequences of Data Processing
description: Authentication service may process registration data in ways that cause unintended consequences for the parent user, such as data breaches, identity theft, or unauthorized profiling.

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Authentication service may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding the collection, storage, and processing of sensitive registration data.

title: Unnecessary Data Collection for Parent Account Storage
description: The Authentication Service may be collecting and storing more parent account data than strictly required for authentication purposes, violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: Assumes the system collects parent account information beyond what is needed for authentication functionality.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: The exact scope of data collected is not fully specified in the flow description.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure Through Stored Metadata
description: The MongoDB users collection may inadvertently disclose implicit information about users through metadata or derived data patterns in the stored parent account information.
assumptions: Assumes the stored data structure may contain or reveal metadata that could be used to link or identify users.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: The exact data structure and metadata implications are not fully specified.

title: Data Integrity Risk in Stored Parent Account Information
description: The stored parent account data in MongoDB could be subject to unauthorized modification, corruption, or tampering, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Assumes the MongoDB storage environment may be vulnerable to unauthorized access or modification.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: The security controls on the MongoDB instance are not specified in the flow description.

title: Data Non-Confidentiality Risk in Stored Parent Account Information
description: The stored parent account data in MongoDB may not be adequately protected against unauthorized access, potentially exposing sensitive user information.
assumptions: Assumes the MongoDB storage may have insufficient access controls or encryption.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: The security measures implemented on the MongoDB instance are not specified in the flow description.

title: Linkability via JWT
description: JWT tokens can be used to link the authenticated user to other activities or systems, potentially enabling tracking across services.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted in a way that preserves their linkability properties.

title: Disclosure of user data
description: Authentication Service shares user data with Parent User, potentially exposing sensitive personal information.
assumptions: User data contains sensitive information that should be protected.

title: Interception during transmission
description: JWT and user data in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to credential compromise.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over a network without guaranteed encryption.

title: Data tampering in transit
description: Data in transit could be modified or tampered with, potentially altering authentication credentials or user data.
assumptions: No integrity protection is guaranteed during data transmission.

title: Linkability at destination
description: Parent User receives JWT and user data that could be used to link them to other authentication events or systems.
assumptions: Parent User has access to the JWT and user data.

title: Unintended use of data
description: Parent User may use the received authentication data in unintended ways, potentially violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Parent User has discretion over how to use the received data.

title: Child User Information Leakage During Login
description: Child user may inadvertently share sensitive information (parent email, password) during login process, potentially exposing personal data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Child user may not fully understand privacy implications of login process

title: Data in Transit Information Leakage
description: Login credentials (parent email, password) transmitted over network may be intercepted by unauthorized parties, especially if encryption is not properly implemented.
assumptions: Data transmitted without adequate encryption or over insecure channels

title: Authentication Service Data Processing Leakage
description: Authentication service may process login credentials in a way that exposes sensitive information to unauthorized parties during processing or storage.
assumptions: Authentication service may not have adequate access controls or encryption for credential processing

title: Authentication Service Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Authentication service may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding handling of child user data and login credentials.
assumptions: Authentication service may not have adequate privacy compliance measures in place

title: JWT token linkage to child identity
description: The JWT token containing child user type information could be used to link the child to other data or profiles, enabling cross-referencing and identity tracking.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted with child profile information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profiles
description: Child profile information shared with the authentication service could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the service is compromised or misused.
assumptions: Child profiles contain sensitive personal information

title: Metadata linkage during transmission
description: Data in transit (JWT and child profiles) may contain metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them, enabling tracking across systems.
assumptions: Transmission metadata is not encrypted or anonymized

title: Data interception during transmission
description: JWT tokens and child profiles transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to potential identity theft or profile manipulation.
assumptions: Transmission channel may not be fully secured

title: Child user linkage to external data
description: The child user receiving JWT and profile information could link this data to other external data sources, enabling cross-referencing and identity tracking.
assumptions: Child user has access to other data sources

title: Unauthorized disclosure by child user
description: The child user could disclose the received JWT and profile information to unauthorized parties, leading to potential misuse of child identity.
assumptions: Child user may not be bound by privacy obligations

title: Linking Parent to Child via Profile Data
description: The data flow transmits child profile information (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) that can be used to link the parent user to the child, potentially revealing family relationships and enabling profiling of family units.
assumptions: Assumes the data may be accessible to third parties or used for cross-referencing with other datasets.

title: Parent Sharing Child's Identifying Information
description: The parent user shares personally identifiable information (PII) including government ID, which could be used to identify the child and potentially link to other records.
assumptions: Assumes the parent may not be fully aware of the implications of sharing this sensitive data.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: The child profile management process may disclose child information to unauthorized parties, including government agencies, insurers, or third-party data brokers.
assumptions: Assumes the process may have inadequate access controls or data sharing agreements.

title: Child Identification via Government ID
description: The government ID used in the child profile can be used to uniquely identify the child across systems, potentially enabling tracking and profiling.
assumptions: Assumes the government ID is a unique identifier that can be cross-referenced with other databases.

title: Unauthorized Data Access from Data Store
description: MongoDB data store may have insufficient access controls allowing unauthorized parties to access child profile data through direct database access, API endpoints, or backup mechanisms.

title: Data Integrity Compromise at Data Store
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be modified, corrupted, or deleted by unauthorized actors through direct database access or through compromised application code.

title: Excessive Data Collection at Source
description: Child Profile Management process may collect more personal data than strictly necessary for profile storage, violating data minimization principles.

title: Data Linkability through Flow Metadata
description: Data flow metadata (timestamps, IP addresses, access patterns) could be used to link child profiles to specific individuals or correlate with other data sources.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Data Storage
description: MongoDB storage of child profile data may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR) regarding data retention, access controls, and security requirements.

title: Improper personal data management by child user
description: Child user may share personal data (name, age, location, preferences) for video search without proper consent or understanding of privacy implications, leading to non-compliance with child data protection regulations.
assumptions: Child users may not fully understand privacy implications of sharing personal data for video search functionality.

title: Data deduplication via metadata
description: Data in transit may contain metadata about the parties (child user and video service) that could be used to link or identify them, potentially enabling profiling or tracking across services.
assumptions: Network metadata may contain information about the communicating parties that could be exploited for identification.

title: Improper personal data management by video service
description: Video Management Service may store or process child user data in a manner that violates child data protection regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K), including inadequate data retention policies or insufficient consent mechanisms.
assumptions: Video service may not have appropriate safeguards for handling child user data.

title: Data confidentiality breach at destination
description: Personal data received from child user may be accessed by unauthorized parties at the video management service, leading to potential data breaches or unauthorized disclosure of child information.
assumptions: Video service may have inadequate access controls or security measures for protecting child user data.

title: Identifying information in video metadata
description: Video metadata traveling with the data flow contains identifying information (timestamps, location, user identifiers) that can be used to link or identify individuals.
assumptions: Video metadata includes temporal and spatial information that may identify individuals.

title: Data disclosure through storage
description: Storing video metadata and files in MongoDB collection may result in implicit disclosure of personal data if the storage is accessed by unauthorized parties or if data is shared with third parties.
assumptions: MongoDB storage may be accessed by unauthorized parties or data may be shared with third parties.

title: Identifying information in metadata collection
description: Video Management Service may be collecting and including identifying information in video metadata when storing videos, potentially exceeding necessary data collection.
assumptions: Video Management Service collects metadata that includes identifying information about individuals.

title: Unauthorized access to child profile data
description: Stored child search and watch history could be accessed by unauthorized parties through database vulnerabilities, weak access controls, or insider threats.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB access controls are properly configured and monitored.

title: Metadata leakage during data transmission
description: Data flow metadata (e.g., timestamps, packet sizes, IP addresses) could be used to link or identify users, even if content is encrypted.
assumptions: Assumes standard network transmission without additional metadata protection.

title: Excessive data collection at source
description: Process may collect more child search and watch history than strictly required by the minimality principle, increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: Assumes current data collection scope exceeds minimum necessary for the stated purpose.

title: Unauthorized data access to stored profiles
description: Stored child profile data could be accessed by unauthorized users through database vulnerabilities, weak authentication, or privilege escalation.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB authentication and authorization mechanisms are properly implemented.

title: Data loss or corruption of child profiles
description: Stored child search and watch history could be lost due to system failures, hardware issues, or improper backup procedures.
assumptions: Assumes standard data loss prevention measures are in place.

title: Regulatory non-compliance for children's data
description: Storage of child search and watch history may violate GDPR/CPRA requirements for special category data or COPPA compliance for children's online services.
assumptions: Assumes current data handling practices may not fully comply with applicable regulations.

title: Unintended video data sharing
description: Parent user may inadvertently share sensitive or private video content without fully understanding the implications of the upload action.
assumptions: User may not be aware of the full scope of data being shared or the potential consequences.

title: Non-compliant data sharing
description: Parent user may share video data in violation of applicable privacy policies or regulatory requirements.
assumptions: User may not be fully informed about privacy obligations or may intentionally bypass compliance measures.

title: Data integrity during transmission
description: Video data may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during transmission from Parent User to Video Management Service.
assumptions: No encryption or integrity protection is in place for the data flow.

title: Identification via metadata
description: Meta-data about the parties (Parent User and Video Management Service) in the data flow may be used to link or identify them.
assumptions: Transmission metadata may contain identifying information about the communicating parties.

title: Unintended video processing
description: Video Management Service may process video data without explicit user consent or in ways not authorized by the user.
assumptions: Service may have broad access to video content beyond what was explicitly requested.

title: Non-compliant video data management
description: Video Management Service may manage video data in violation of applicable privacy regulations or data protection policies.
assumptions: Service may not have adequate privacy controls or compliance measures in place.

title: Unauthorized video sharing
description: Video Management Service may share video content with child user without proper authorization or consent, potentially violating child protection regulations.
assumptions: Assumes video content is 'approved' but authorization verification may not be complete.

title: Non-compliant video sharing
description: Video Management Service may share video content in violation of applicable privacy regulations or data protection laws.
assumptions: Assumes service operates under some regulatory framework.

title: Video data integrity during transmission
description: Video content may be intercepted, modified, or corrupted during transmission from Video Management Service to child user.
assumptions: Assumes video is transmitted over network without end-to-end encryption.

title: Unauthorized interception of video stream
description: Video stream may be intercepted by unauthorized third parties during transmission, potentially exposing sensitive content.
assumptions: Assumes video may contain sensitive or private information.

title: Unauthorized access to video content
description: Child user may access video content without proper authorization or in violation of intended usage.
assumptions: Assumes child user may have multiple access points or devices.

title: Non-compliant video consumption
description: Child user may consume video content in violation of applicable privacy regulations or data protection laws.
assumptions: Assumes child user may have limited understanding of privacy regulations.

title: Explicit disclosure of child browsing data to AI engine
description: The MongoDB childprofiles DataStore explicitly shares child browsing data with the AI Recommendation Engine by design. This constitutes a data disclosure where personal data about children is transferred across a system boundary to an external processing component.

title: Data in transit metadata exposure
description: Data flowing from DS2 to P4 in transit may expose metadata about the parties involved (source and destination identifiers, timestamps, etc.) that could be used to link or identify the data subjects or their browsing patterns.

title: AI engine processing and potential re-disclosure
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may process the child browsing data and potentially re-disclose it to third parties or use it to generate recommendations that could be shared externally, creating additional data disclosure pathways.

title: Explicit disclosure of browsing data to third-party advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine intentionally shares browsing data with third-party advertisers, constituting an explicit data disclosure. This transfer of personal data across a boundary may violate the minimality principle if browsing data is not strictly required for the intended purpose.
assumptions: Browsing data contains personal information about user behavior and preferences

title: Data in transit may expose metadata about parties
description: The data flow itself may contain metadata about the parties involved (source and destination), which could be used to link or identify users. This is a data-centric threat at the flow level.
assumptions: Data in transit may include headers or metadata revealing the nature of the data transfer

title: Third-party advertisers may further disclose browsing data
description: Upon receipt of browsing data, third-party advertisers may process, store, or further disclose this data to other parties, potentially leading to additional data disclosures beyond the original transfer.
assumptions: Advertisers have their own data handling practices that may include further sharing or processing of received data

title: Unauthorized access to stored government ID images
description: The File System (DS4) may allow unauthorized access to stored government ID images, potentially leading to data disclosure to unauthorized parties. This violates the minimality principle and could result in identity theft or fraud.

title: Data confidentiality breach at storage
description: Stored government ID images may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, compromising the confidentiality of personal data. This could lead to identity theft, fraud, or other privacy violations.

title: Data integrity compromise at storage
description: Stored government ID images may be tampered with, corrupted, or altered by unauthorized parties, compromising the integrity of the personal data. This could lead to fraudulent use of altered documents.

title: Explicit data disclosure to File System
description: The Authentication Service (P1) shares government ID images with the File System (DS4) for storage. While this is an intended action, it represents an explicit disclosure of personal data that must be justified by necessity and minimized.

title: Data linkage through metadata in transit
description: Data in transit (DF15) may contain metadata about the parties involved (e.g., timestamps, IP addresses, user identifiers) that could be used to link or identify individuals, even if the actual image content is not compromised.

title: JWT Disclosure at Source
description: Authentication Service shares JWT tokens that may contain sensitive user information, creating risk of disclosure if sharing mechanism is compromised.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity and session information

title: Unintended JWT Storage
description: Authentication Service may store JWT in localStorage without proper security controls, creating risk of unintended access or exposure.
assumptions: JWT stored in localStorage without encryption or access controls

title: JWT Interception in Transit
description: JWT tokens in transit from Authentication Service to Browser localStorage may be intercepted by malicious actors.
assumptions: Data flow occurs over network without proper encryption

title: JWT Disclosure at Destination
description: Browser localStorage may be accessed by malicious actors through XSS attacks or browser vulnerabilities, leading to JWT disclosure.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to malicious JavaScript or browser exploits

title: Unintended JWT Access
description: JWT stored in localStorage may be accessed unintentionally by other applications or scripts with access to the browser context.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript running in the same context

title: Child History Data Linking via Flow Meta-data
description: The data flow DF17 transmits child history data from Process P3 to External Entity EE1. During transmission, meta-data about the parties (e.g., timestamps, identifiers, routing information) could be used to link this child to other data about the child or parent, potentially building unwanted profiles or revealing additional information about the data subject.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow may contain or be associated with identifiers that could be used for linking purposes.

title: Parent User Information Disclosure of Child History
description: The parent user (EE1) receives child history data. If this data contains sensitive information beyond what the parent should know, or if the parent is not authorized to receive this information, this could lead to privacy violations through information disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the parent may not have explicit authorization to receive all child history data, or the data may contain information beyond parental scope.

title: Unauthorized Child History Sharing by Process
description: The Child Profile Management process (P3) may share child history data without proper authorization or without the parent's explicit consent, leading to unintended data sharing.
assumptions: Assumes the process may lack proper authorization controls or consent mechanisms for data sharing.
